ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the input X(t) enters from the left and is divided into two paths: the upper branch is sent directly to the summing device on the right and is marked with a positive sign at the summing device; the lower branch first passes through a delay block labeled Delay = T0, then is sent to the same summing device and is marked with a negative sign at the summing device; the summing device output is Y(t). Therefore from the figure the system relationship is Y(t)=X(t)-X(t-T0). Reasoning: The output autocorrelation function by definition is R_Y(tau)=E[Y(t)Y(t+tau)]. Substituting Y(t)=X(t)-X(t-T0), and Y(t+tau)=X(t+tau)-X(t+tau-T0), gives R_Y(tau)=E[(X(t)-X(t-T0))(X(t+tau)-X(t+tau-T0))]. Expanding gives E[X(t)X(t+tau)] - E[X(t)X(t+tau-T0)] - E[X(t-T0)X(t+tau)] + E[X(t-T0)X(t+tau-T0)]. Since X(t) is a wide-sense stationary process, these four terms are respectively R_X(tau), R_X(tau-T0), R_X(tau+T0), R_X(tau). So R_Y(tau)=2R_X(tau)-R_X(tau-T0)-R_X(tau+T0).
